name: Workshop Practices Lab
sem: I or II (group-wise; alternative to Engineering Graphics & Design Lab MEP-002)
objectives: Ability to prepare simple objects using machines and machine tools.
Make students aware of fundamental operations of manufacturing an engineering component, enhance visualization and motivate them to innovate.
outcomes: CO1 Capability to identify hand tools and instruments for machining and other workshop practices.
CO2 Obtain basic skills in the trades of fitting, carpentry, welding and machining.
CO3 Acquire measuring skills using standard workshop instruments and tools.
CO4 Gain eye-hand coordination, enhance psychomotor skills and attitude.
CO5 Apply basic electrical engineering knowledge for house wiring practice.
ref: A course in Workshop Technology Vol I and Vol II by Prof. B.S. Raghuwanshi, Dhanpat Rai & Co.(P) Ltd.
Elements of Workshop Technology Vol I and Vol II by S.K. Hajara Choudhury, A.K. Hajara Choudhury & Nirjhar Roy; Media Promoters & Publishers Pvt. Ltd, Mumbai.
Workshop Technology Part 1, Part 2 & Part 3 by W.A.J. Chapman; CBS Publishers & Distributors, New Delhi.
note: Marks 50 sessional + 50 external = 100 for the combined MEP-002/MEP-003 row (credit 2, L-T-P 0-1-2).

exps.title: Tutorial
exps.aim: Manufacturing methods: casting, forming, machining, joining, advanced manufacturing methods, CNC machining and additive manufacturing; Fitting operations and power tools; Electrical and electronics; Study of carpentry tools, equipment and different joints; Plastic moulding and glass cutting; Metal casting; Welding (arc and gas welding) and brazing.
exps.formula: Manufacturing classes: casting (shape by pouring), forming (plastic deformation), machining (material removal), joining (welding, brazing, soldering)
viva: Name the four basic manufacturing process groups.
Casting, forming, machining and joining.
What is additive manufacturing?
Building a part layer by layer from a digital model, e.g. 3D printing.

exps.title: Machine shop
exps.aim: Study of machine tools in particular lathe machine; demonstration of different operations on lathe machine; practice of facing, plane turning, step turning, taper turning, knurling and parting; study of quick return mechanism in shaper; to make a machined component using lathe with mild steel round bar or hexagonal bar comprising common turning operations with reference to drawing given in the manual.
exps.apparatus: Lathe machine, single-point cutting tools, chuck, vernier caliper, shaper, knurling tool, parting tool
exps.formula: Cutting speed V = πDN/1000 m/min (D in mm, N in rpm)
viva: Name the main parts of a lathe.
Bed, headstock, tailstock, carriage, lead screw and tool post.
Why is a quick return mechanism used in a shaper?
The return stroke is faster than the cutting stroke, saving idle time.

exps.title: Fitting and sheet metal shop
exps.aim: Study of fitting and sheet metal shop tools; making a perfect male-female joint; simple exercise involving drilling/tapping/dieing; to make a sheet metal component with galvanized iron sheet as per the drawing provided in the manual having spot welding joint.
exps.apparatus: Hacksaw, files, try square, scriber, surface plate, vice, drill, taps and dies, tin snips, GI sheet, spot welding machine
exps.formula: Tap drill size ≈ major diameter − pitch
viva: What is the use of a tap and a die?
A tap cuts internal threads; a die cuts external threads.
Why is a hacksaw blade fitted with teeth pointing forward?
It cuts on the forward stroke only.

exps.title: Carpentry
exps.aim: Study of tools and operation and carpentry joints; simple exercise using jack plane; to prepare half-lap corner joint, mortise and tenon joints as per drawing provided in the lab manual; simple exercise on woodworking lathe.
exps.apparatus: Jack plane, tenon saw, chisel, mallet, marking gauge, try square, wood, woodworking lathe
exps.formula: Tenon thickness ≈ one-third of stock thickness (rule of thumb)
viva: Name some carpentry joints.
Lap, mortise and tenon, dovetail, mitre, dado.
What is seasoning of timber?
Removing moisture from timber to prevent warping and shrinkage.

exps.title: Electrical and electronics
exps.aim: Soldering and desoldering application in electronic equipment; introduction to house wiring and different types of cables; types of power supply, types of motors and starters, distribution of power supply and electric wiring symbols.
exps.apparatus: Soldering iron, solder wire, flux, desoldering pump, wire stripper, cables, switches, MCB, lamp holder
exps.formula: Power P = VI; Ohm's law V = IR
viva: Why is flux used in soldering?
It removes oxide and helps solder wet the joint.
What does an MCB do?
Protects the circuit by tripping on overload or short circuit.

exps.title: Welding shop
exps.aim: Instruction of BI standards and reading of welding drawings; to prepare butt and lap joints using metal arc welding machine as per given manual and drawing; hands-on experience with MIG, TIG and gas welding.
exps.apparatus: Arc welding machine, electrode, electrode holder, chipping hammer, wire brush, face shield, gloves, MIG/TIG/gas welding set
exps.formula: Heat input H = (V × I × 60)/(1000 × S) kJ/mm, S = travel speed in mm/min
viva: Why is a face shield with a dark glass used?
To protect eyes and face from arc radiation and spatter.
What gases are used in gas welding?
Oxygen and acetylene.

exps.title: Foundry shop
exps.aim: Study of tools and operations; demo of mould preparation; practice and preparation of mould of any pattern; casting of any simple pattern.
exps.apparatus: Moulding box (cope and drag), pattern, moulding sand, rammer, riddle, trowel, vent wire, furnace, ladle
exps.formula: Pattern is made larger than the casting by the shrinkage allowance
viva: What is a pattern?
A replica of the casting used to make the mould cavity.
Why are vent holes made in a mould?
To let gases escape during pouring.

exps.title: Smithy shop
exps.aim: Study of tools and operations; simple exercises based on black smithy operations such as upsetting, drawing down, punching, bending, fullering and swaging.
exps.apparatus: Hearth, anvil, tongs, hammers, flatter, swage, fuller, punch, chisels
exps.formula: Upsetting increases cross-section and reduces length; drawing down does the reverse
viva: What is upsetting?
Increasing the cross-section of a heated rod by hammering it along its length.
What is swaging?
Reducing or finishing round work using a swage tool.

exps.title: Minor Project
exps.aim: To make a minor project by the students in batches comprising the operations performed in different shops.
exps.apparatus: Tools and machines of the machine, fitting, carpentry, welding, foundry and smithy shops
exps.formula: Plan: drawing, material list, sequence of operations, finishing and inspection
viva: How do you plan a job across shops?
Prepare drawing and bill of material, choose sequence of operations, and inspect each stage.
Why is safety important?
To prevent injuries: wear PPE and follow shop rules.
